info.title: Nizam API — Carrier
info.description:
The **Nizam Carrier Portal API** is the surface for Tier-2 carriers, independent fleet operators that accept delegated lanes from a primary Nizam Organization. Use this API to view delegated work, accept or decline lanes, see settlement, and read the fleet you operate against.

This is one of the [audience-scoped Nizam APIs](https://docs.nizam.ai/api/overview). It shares the wire-level conventions (RFC 9457 errors, cursor pagination, expand grammar) with every other Nizam audience; see the [API conventions reference](https://docs.nizam.ai/api/conventions) for the canonical description. This page covers what's specific to the Carrier Portal.

## Audience

This API ships in the **Carrier SDK** (`@nizam-os/carrier-sdk` on npm). Consumers are administrators of independent carriers who hold a delegation relationship with a Nizam Organization. The carrier itself operates as its own Nizam Organization; the Carrier Portal is the cross-organization surface they use to interact with primary organizations.

The drivers and runtime-side software employed by the carrier authenticate as **operators** through the [Operator Runtime SDK](https://docs.nizam.ai/operator), not through this portal.

## Authentication

Issued by the **`nizam-carrier-portal`** OAuth client. Authorization Code + PKCE flow.

Obtain the token from the `nizam-carrier-portal` client and send it unchanged as a bearer credential; treat it as opaque. The server scopes every request to your organization and derives your authorization from the token; you never parse it.

## Roles

Single role: `admin`. Worker-level access (driver portal, dispatch board) does not exist on this SDK; those use the Operator Runtime SDK. This separation is intentional: drivers may move between carriers; the operator identity is portable, the carrier admin identity is not.

## Surface

- `/v1/me` and `/v1/invites/accept`: identity and onboarding.
- `/v1/lookups/*`: reference data.
- Carrier-specific surface (delegated lanes, partnership management, settlement) lands as the multi-organization delivery features come online.

## Cross-organization scoping

Carrier operations span organizations by design: a carrier authenticated through `nizam-carrier-portal` reads work delegated to them BY the primary Organization. Through that delegation relationship, the carrier sees only the lanes a primary organization has shared with them, never the primary's full fleet or operations.

## Status

This SDK is narrow today. The carrier surface grows as multi-organization delegation features ship.

get.description: The active organization's files ordered by `created_at` descending by default. `kind` / `status` accept comma-separated values; `subject_type` + `subject_id` narrow to the files documenting one business entity. Pagination is bidirectional (`starting_after` / `ending_before`).

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Filter by file kind. Comma-separated; matched case-insensitively.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by lifecycle status. Comma-separated; matched case-insensitively.

parameters.name: subject_type
parameters.description: Filter by the documented entity's type (pairs with `subject_id`).

parameters.name: subject_id
parameters.description: Filter by the documented entity's id (requires `subject_type`).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order. Allowed fields: `created_at`. Append `:asc` or `:desc` to each field (direction required, e.g. `created_at:desc`), comma-separated for multi-sort; unknown fields or directions are rejected with `400 validation_failed`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Default 20, maximum 100. Out-of-range values are silently clamped; the response body's `limit` field reflects what was applied.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Opaque cursor: return the page starting strictly after this entity in the sort order. Mutually exclusive with `ending_before`.

parameters.name: ending_before
parameters.description: Opaque cursor: return the page ending strictly before this entity in the sort order. Mutually exclusive with `starting_after`.

post.description: Validates the declaration against the kind's policy (allowed portals, content types, size ceiling, organization quota), pre-reserves the final file id, and returns presigned part URLs. PUT each part's bytes directly to its URL (repeating the part's `headers` verbatim) and keep each response's `ETag` for completion. Sessions expire after 24h; the part URLs sooner. Re-issue them via the resume endpoint.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. Supply a UUID (canonical 8-4-4-4-12 form; lowercase v4 recommended) to make this operation idempotent: the same key on a retry replays the original outcome instead of creating a second resource. 2xx successes and deliberate 4xx domain rejections are cached and replayed for 24h when the request body matches; transient 5xx responses are never cached, so a retry with the same key re-executes. A malformed key is rejected with 400 `idempotency.invalid_key`; reusing a key with a different request body is 409 `idempotency.key_conflict`; a key still in flight is 409 `idempotency.in_progress`. Omit the header and the operation behaves like any other write.

get.description:
Returns every credential registered on the AUTHENTICATED user's account — password, authenticator app, recovery codes, and passkeys — each with the name the member gave it and when it was registered. The subject is pinned server-side; there is no id in the path.

Read this to decide what to offer on a security screen: whether to prompt for a first authenticator or an additional one, whether recovery codes are worth offering (they are only useful once a second factor exists), and which credentials can be removed.

Registering and removing credentials both happen at the identity provider rather than through this API, via Keycloak's application-initiated actions — so the member re-authenticates on the provider's own hardened pages and no credential material ever transits this API. The `id` here is what identifies a credential to those flows.

Secret material is never returned: the shared secret, password hash parameters and passkey public key are dropped server-side and are not part of this shape.

delete.description:
Turns two-step verification OFF for the AUTHENTICATED user by removing every second-factor credential they hold: all authenticator apps AND the recovery-code set. The subject is pinned server-side; there is no id in the path.

Both go, because the identity provider has no "second factor: off" switch — the second step is required whenever the account holds any credential that can satisfy it. Removing the authenticators alone would not disable anything; it would promote the recovery codes from a fallback to the only accepted factor, and since each code works exactly once the account becomes unreachable when the set runs out. Removing a single credential (one authenticator among several) is a different operation and happens at the identity provider, not here.

Idempotent: an account that already has two-step off answers 204, as does a repeated or retried request. Sign-in falls back to the password, plus any passkey the member has registered.

get.description: The caller's own notifications ordered by `created_at` descending by default. `status` selects the segment: `all` (default; the active inbox, non-archived), `unread`, `read`, or `archived`. `category` and `kind` accept comma-separated values and AND on top of the segment; `q` matches the notification title/body. `since=` (RFC 3339) returns only items at/after the instant for incremental catch-up after a reconnect. Pagination is bidirectional (`starting_after` / `ending_before`); cursors are bound to the sort direction that minted them.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Inbox segment. One of: `all` (default: active, non-archived), `unread`, `read`, `archived`.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Filter by category. Comma-separated; values: `transactional`, `operational`, `alert`, `marketing`, `security`, `system`.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Filter by notification kind (wire key). Comma-separated; e.g. `membership.joined`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free-text search over the notification title/body (max 200 chars).

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only notifications created at/after this RFC 3339 instant.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order. Allowed fields: `created_at`. Append `:asc` or `:desc` to each field (direction required, e.g. `created_at:desc`), comma-separated for multi-sort; unknown fields or directions are rejected with `400 validation_failed`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Default 20, maximum 100. Out-of-range values are silently clamped; the response body's `limit` field reflects what was applied.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Opaque cursor: return the page starting strictly after this entity in the sort order. Mutually exclusive with `ending_before`.

parameters.name: ending_before
parameters.description: Opaque cursor: return the page ending strictly before this entity in the sort order. Mutually exclusive with `starting_after`.

get.description:
The signed, DER-encoded CRL naming every revoked certificate that has not yet expired on its own (RFC 5280 §5 permits dropping the rest, which is what keeps the list bounded by the certificate lifetime rather than growing forever). This is the URL Keycloak's X.509 authenticator polls.

An empty list is a normal, successful answer and means nothing is revoked. It is materially different from a failure to fetch, which Keycloak treats as a reason to refuse machine authentication outright — which is also why this endpoint requires no credential: a revocation list that needed one could not be read by the thing deciding whether credentials are valid.

`Cache-Control` is deliberately much shorter than the list's own `nextUpdate`. The former bounds how long an intermediary may serve a copy; the latter is the fail-closed staleness deadline that decides how long an outage may last before every machine is locked out.

post.summary: Exchange an enrolment voucher for a certificate
post.description:
The machine's FIRST credential. The device generates a keypair, keeps the private key, and sends a PKCS#10 signing request together with the single-use voucher it was commissioned with. The EST `/simpleenroll` step.

The certificate's subject is fixed by the voucher, not by the request: nothing a caller sends influences which identity is certified, so a stolen voucher enrols the one machine it was minted for.

**The response is not repeatable.** The voucher is consumed on success and the platform does not store the certificate, so a device that loses this response needs a fresh voucher rather than a retry. Errors: 404 `workload.enrolment_not_found` (unknown or malformed token — never distinguished, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which vouchers exist), 409 `workload.enrolment_already_redeemed` (someone enrolled with this voucher already — treat as an incident), 410 `workload.enrolment_expired` / `workload.enrolment_revoked`, 400 `workload.invalid_signing_request`, 409 `workload.key_already_certified`, 503 `workload.authority_unavailable`.

post.description:
Issues a fresh certificate to a device that presented a currently-valid one over mTLS — the EST `/simplereenroll` step. The presented certificate identifies the caller; the body carries only the new signing request.

The key MUST be newly generated. Re-certifying an existing key would let one compromise survive every rotation, so it is refused with 409 `workload.key_already_certified`.

The previous certificate is deliberately left VALID until it expires on its own. Overlapping validity is what stops a rotation that fails halfway from stranding a vehicle; the short lifetime, not a supersession sweep, is what bounds how long an old key stays useful.

401 `workload.renewal_not_permitted` covers every reason the presented certificate is unacceptable — absent, unknown, revoked, expired, or not byte-identical to one this platform issued. They are not distinguished, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which serials exist.

invited_email.description: Recipient email: canonical lowercase form. Exactly one of `invited_email` / `invited_phone` is set — staff invitations carry the email, operator (driver) enrolments the phone.

invited_phone.description: Recipient phone in E.164 form, for operator (driver) enrolments. Exactly one of `invited_email` / `invited_phone` is set.

role.description: Role the recipient will hold after acceptance.

expires_at.description: When the invite expires. Recipients must accept before then.

accepted_at.description: When the invitation was accepted, if it was.

revoked_at.description: When the invitation was revoked, if it was.

token.description: Bearer secret used to redeem the invite. Returned only on POST /v1/invites, where the sender sees it once; absent from every other response, including the lifecycle verbs.

allowed_transitions.description: Lifecycle statuses an administrator can move this invitation to next, the wire projection of the server-side transition matrix, derived from `status`. Empty once the invitation is settled. Acceptance and expiry never appear: they are the recipient's act and the clock's, not an administrator's.

items.description: A status an administrator may move this invitation to.

FileUploadPart.description: A presigned PUT for one part. Send the raw part bytes; repeat `headers` verbatim; keep the response's `ETag` header for completion.

url.description: Presigned URL to PUT the part's bytes to.

additionalProperties.description: Headers that were signed into the URL; the PUT must repeat them verbatim.

headers.description: Headers that were signed into the URL; the PUT must repeat them verbatim.

url_expires_at.description: When this URL stops working (re-issue via resume).

FileUploadSession.description: A resumable multipart upload in flight. The browser PUTs each part directly to the presigned URL (echoing the part's `headers` verbatim), persists the returned ETags, and completes the session with the full part list. `file_id` is the id the finished file WILL carry, safe to build optimistic UI against.

id.description: Session id: the handle for resume / complete / cancel.

file_id.description: Pre-reserved id of the file this upload will become.

part_size_bytes.description: Nominal part size; every part except the last must be exactly this size.

bytes_uploaded.description: Bytes confirmed so far (client-reported, re-verified at completion).

expires_at.description: Deadline: the session expires and is swept if not completed by then.

FileDownloadUrl.description: A short-lived URL granting read access to a file's bytes. Fetch it promptly; request a fresh grant after expiry.

url.description: The URL to GET the bytes from.

InitiateFileUploadRequest.description: Declares an upload and requests presigned part URLs.

kind.description: What the bytes are for the platform: fixes the policy applied to them.

subject_type.description: Type of the business entity this file documents (optional at upload time; can also be attached later).

subject_id.description: Id of the business entity this file documents. Requires subject_type.

filename.description: Original filename; served back via Content-Disposition on download.

content_type.description: Declared MIME type. Must be on the kind's allow-list; re-verified by server-side detection at completion.

size_bytes.description: Exact byte size of the file. Verified against storage at completion.

checksum_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the content as 64 lowercase hex characters (compute with crypto.subtle.digest). Re-verified server-side by the scan pipeline.

File.description: A stored file's metadata: what it is (kind), who uploaded it, integrity (checksum), lifecycle (status + scan verdict + retention), and what business entity it documents (subject). The bytes themselves are served only through short-lived download URLs.

id.description: Stable file id (pre-reserved at upload initiation).

uploader_id.description: Uploading user. Null for system-generated artifacts.

kind.description: What the bytes are for the platform: fixes the size/type/visibility/scan/retention policy applied to this file.

subject_type.description: Type of the business entity this file documents.

subject_id.description: Id of the business entity this file documents.

parent_file_id.description: For derived files (thumbnails): the original this one was rendered from.

original_filename.description: Client-supplied filename, served back via Content-Disposition on download.

declared_content_type.description: MIME type declared by the uploader at initiation.

sniffed_content_type.description: MIME type detected server-side from the bytes (Tika). Null when detection was inconclusive.

size_bytes.description: Object size in bytes, storage-confirmed at completion.

checksum_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the content, 64 lowercase hex characters.

status.description: Lifecycle: `active` (serving), `quarantined` (malware-positive), `deleted` (bytes purged, row retained under regulatory hold).

visibility.description: Access posture of the bytes, fixed by the kind's policy.

virus_scan_status.description: Malware-scan verdict. Bytes are downloadable only on `clean` or `skipped`.

virus_scanned_at.description: When the scan verdict was produced.

expires_at.description: When this file becomes eligible for the lifecycle sweep (TTL kinds).

retention_until.description: Regulatory hold: the file cannot be deleted before this instant.

CompleteFileUploadRequest.description: Confirms every uploaded part to assemble the file.

FileUploadPartReport.description: The storage ETag received for one uploaded part.

part_number.description: 1-based part number from the initiation layout.

etag.description: The ETag header value returned by the part's PUT (quotes optional).

User.description: The current authenticated user: identity + portal context + login activity.

id.description: Stable UUID. Equal to the Keycloak `sub` claim.

portal.description: Which portal issued the bearer token used for this request.

organization_id.description: Keycloak Organization id the user belongs to. Null for cross-tenant platform admins.

items.description: Realm roles (flat, e.g. `platform_admin`) plus portal-scoped client roles (prefixed, e.g. `dashboard:dispatcher`).

permissions.description: The caller's effective permission ids for the active organization (epic #317): the union of catalog grants for every role they hold. Gate actions on these (`can("asset:create")`) rather than role strings, so frontend and backend reference the one catalog and cannot drift. Coarse and instance-independent; per-instance authority ('may delete THIS asset') is enforced server-side at the mutation, never precomputed here.

email.description: Email shadowed from Keycloak. Null until the user completes a profile.

email_verified.description: Whether Keycloak has verified the user owns their email (OIDC `email_verified`). Read from the live token, not the shadow, an auth-time fact. Drives the profile UI's verified badge vs. the 'verify email' action.

name.description: Display name. Seeded from Keycloak at first login; thereafter the user edits it via PATCH /v1/me (written through to Keycloak).

phone.description: Contact phone in E.164 format (app-managed via PATCH /v1/me). Null until the user sets one. Setting a phone stores an unverified contact number; it becomes a sign-in identifier only after a possession proof.

phone_verified_at.description: When the current phone was verified by a possession proof. Null while the phone is unverified contact data. Editing the phone clears it.

locale.description: Preferred UI language as a BCP 47 tag (app-managed via PATCH /v1/me). Null until the user sets one.

timezone.description: Preferred IANA timezone (app-managed via PATCH /v1/me). Null until the user sets one.

last_login_at.description: Timestamp of this login. Null only on the very first call before provisioning completes.

login_count.description: Total logins observed by this service.

profile_picture_file_id.description: File id of the current profile picture (epic #151 / #166); null until one is uploaded. Request bytes via the files download-url endpoint, or let `GET /users/{id}/profile-picture` pick the nearest thumbnail.

UpdateMeRequest.description: Self-service profile update for the authenticated user.

name.description: New display name. Omit to leave unchanged.

phone.description: New contact phone in E.164 format. Omit to leave unchanged. Stored as unverified contact data: changing the number clears any verification, and a number becomes a sign-in identifier only after a possession proof.

locale.description: New preferred UI language as a BCP 47 tag. Omit to leave unchanged.

timezone.description: New preferred IANA timezone identifier. Omit to leave unchanged.

NotificationPreferenceItem.description: Desired state of one (kind, channel) preference.

enabled.description: Whether the user wants this kind on this channel.

QuietHours.description: A do-not-disturb window in wall-clock time within a zone.

timezone.description: IANA zone id the wall-clock is read in.

UpdateNotificationPreferences.description: A batch of preference overrides to upsert.

preferences.description: The overrides to apply; each fully declares one (kind, channel).

NotificationPreference.description: A user's explicit per-kind × channel override.

enabled.description: Whether the kind is enabled on this channel.

preferences.description: The user's explicit per-kind × channel overrides.

TaskAttemptPhoto.description: A proof-of-delivery photo captured during a task attempt.

file_id.description: Central file id: request bytes via the files download-url endpoint.

downloadable.description: May the bytes be served right now (scan verdict + lifecycle)?

created_at.description: When the photo row was recorded.

max_dimension.description: Bounding-box size the variant was rendered into (px).

file_id.description: The variant's file id: request bytes via the files download-url endpoint.

SharedConversation.description: A read-only, redacted view of a shared conversation.

title.description: Conversation title, or null if untitled.

SharedConversationMessage.description: One message in a shared conversation.
